- **Story:** As Dana, I want to install Avowry as one native binary with a one-line script, so that I can compile Avowry source on a machine without .NET.
- **Consumer value:** Dana compiles Avowry source on a machine that has no .NET; we see it when a clean Linux container with no SDK installs with one line and `avowry build Tasks.avowry` exits 0 and prints the C# project path.
- **Acceptance criteria (Given/When/Then; at most 3, each failing on partial work):**
  1. Scenario: [O][S][Z] one binary, no .NET
     Given Dana's stack is not fixed and this Given is a clean Linux container with no .NET
     When she installs Avowry with a one-line script and runs `avowry build Tasks.avowry`
     Then the command exits 0 and prints the C# project path
  2. Scenario: [I] one-line install on PATH
     Given that one-line install script
     When she runs it on that container
     Then `avowry` is on PATH and `avowry --version` prints a version
  3. Scenario: [B] same compile result as today's CLI
     Given the native binary and today's JIT-built CLI
     When both run `avowry build Tasks.avowry`
     Then the generated C# project path and files match
  Letters that do not apply: [M] extra platforms and the winget, Homebrew and Scoop names are v0.1 bar 7 one-way doors left to later cards; [E] AOT and install failure modes stay unknowns until the AOT check runs.
